title: Does a hand-written flexing-sheet plant agree with MuJoCo, and do its sim-to-sim transfer failures hold there?
summary: buildbot-skills reported that sheet-following skills tuned on a rigid-sheet model fail on a held-out plant with a flexing board, sensing delay and actuator lag, but that plant was my own numpy Lagrangian. Here the same plant is rebuilt in MuJoCo 3.16 (two boxes on hinges, a spring-damper at the midline, RK4, the pin's acceleration put into gravity) with the same Python controller, delay and actuator code, and the 13 policies of buildbot-skills are run on 200 shared random worlds each. The pass-fail label agrees on 99.8% of the 2600 episodes (at worst 99% for one policy); no policy's pass rate differs between engines by more than 1 point; the share of unstable episodes agrees for 12 of 13 policies. Median peak-tilt difference is 0.0005–0.003° for the usable (B-trained) gains and up to 0.7° for marginally stable gains. So the transfer failure is not an artefact of the hand-derived equations. It does not test the shared inputs: delay (0–30 ms), actuator lag, sheet stiffness (150–6000 N m/rad) and the planar two-force-point abstraction are the same ranges of mine and none was measured.
lede: does the hand-written flexing-sheet plant of buildbot-skills agree with MuJoCo? Pass/fail labels agree on 99.8% of 2600 episodes across 13 policies, so the sim-to-sim transfer failure (0-11% vs 81% where tuned) is not an artefact of my equations.
